title: Vitamin D: Which Foods Have the Most and Why It Is Often Low

seo.title: Vitamin D Foods: Best Sources and Why It Runs Low
seo.meta_description: Fatty fish, fish-liver oils, egg yolk, and fortified foods provide vitamin D. Few foods naturally contain much, which makes dietary intake relatively difficult.
seo.search_intent: Identify the main food sources of vitamin D and explain why dietary intake is often low.

excerpt: Fatty fish are among the few naturally concentrated sources of vitamin D; egg yolk, liver, and some UV-exposed mushrooms provide smaller amounts, while fortified milk and other products can contribute substantially. There simply are not many naturally rich everyday foods.
content_html:
Vitamin D is unusual because the body can make some in skin exposed to UVB, while the list of foods naturally rich in it is short. A varied diet therefore does not automatically mean a high vitamin D intake.

Fatty fish lead the natural-food list

Salmon, trout, mackerel, herring, and similar fish can provide several micrograms per serving, with substantial variation by species and origin. Fish-liver oils are even more concentrated but are consumed in much smaller amounts.

Egg yolk and liver contain modest amounts. Mushrooms exposed to ultraviolet light can provide vitamin D2. In the U.S., fortified milk and selected plant beverages, cereals, and juices can make a meaningful contribution because fortification is common.

Why food alone can be challenging

The U.S. Recommended Dietary Allowance is 15 micrograms, or 600 IU, per day for most adults through age 70. Reaching that consistently requires regular use of the relatively few rich or fortified sources.

Vitamin D status also depends on sun exposure, season, latitude, skin pigmentation, age, and health factors. Blood-test interpretation and supplement dosing are medical questions, not something a food ranking can settle.

faq.question: What food is highest in vitamin D?
faq.answer: Fatty fish and fish-liver oils are among the most concentrated natural sources.

faq.question: Do eggs have vitamin D?
faq.answer: Yes, mainly in the yolk, but a typical egg contributes less than a serving of fatty fish.

faq.question: Do mushrooms contain vitamin D?
faq.answer: Some do, especially mushrooms exposed to ultraviolet light, which can accumulate vitamin D2.
